subject: Zero-downtime cutover rehearsal: bridge notes, warmstart, and rollback triggers
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, julie@acme-ops.com, ops-lead@finco.com
Cc: oncall@carrier-networks.com
Date: 2027-12-07T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Zero-downtime cutover rehearsal: bridge notes, warmstart, and rollback triggers

Team / partners —

Thanks for lining up to run the zero-downtime rehearsal tomorrow (08 Dec). Goal: exercise the bridge, validate traffic-shift controls, confirm warmstart (KV cache priming) effectiveness, and rehearse the rollback trigger path without impacting production. High-level timeline attached in traffic-shift-plan-v3.pdf.

Quick asks before the bridge:
- Acme: can you confirm BGP flaps window is disabled for our prefixes and that your ACLs are in the temporary allow-list?
- Carrier: confirm the mirroring span will be active for the first 30 minutes and collection is going to our collector (oncall@carrier-networks.com).
- Ops: please pre-provision the two failback routes and have the rollback playbook (section 4) open.

On the runbook side I put the warmstart steps in kv-cache-warmstart-steps.md — these are low-risk: start with a capped KV window, verify hit rate, then expand TTL. Targets for success: 90% hit-rate on hot prefixes within 10 minutes and latency <= 50ms p50 on inference tail for the initial steady state.

Bridge dial-in: +1 415 555 0123 (pin 8342) at 09:00 PT. We'll run a 45-minute scripted rehearsal and then a 30-minute live observation period. If anything exceeds the rollback thresholds below, initiate immediate rollback and notify stakeholders.

Rollback thresholds (short list):
- 5xxs > 1% sustained over 5 minutes
- End-to-end median latency increase > 2x baseline for 10 minutes
- KV cache hit-rate < 60% for 10 minutes post-warmstart

Please review attachments and reply with any blockers. I'll be on the bridge and monitoring dashboards.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: traffic-shift-plan-v3.pdf, kv-cache-warmstart-steps.md
From: Julie Park <julie@acme-ops.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops-lead@finco.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, oncall@carrier-networks.com
Date: 2027-12-07T18:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Zero-downtime cutover rehearsal: bridge notes, warmstart, and rollback triggers

Sean —

Thanks for the clear plan. A quick status from Acme side: BGP flaps window is scheduled and should be closed by 07:30 PT tomorrow; I asked netops to keep a one-hour guard window. ACLs have been updated to include your test IPs (see ACL ticket NET-784).

A couple of clarifications:
- For KV warmstart, do you want us to seed the prefix set from our side (we have a hot-keys export) or should Redwood perform a synthetic priming run? Our preference is Acme seeds hot-keys and you expand TTLs; that minimizes cross-network traffic.
- Regarding the mirroring span, we will mirror only HTTP/HTTPS on the control VLAN — confirm this is sufficient for your observability needs.

We will join the 09:00 PT bridge and have our ops lead on the line. If you want us to run a preflight mirroring test at 08:45 PT we can do that.

Julie
Julie Park
SRE Manager, Acme Financial

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: julie@acme-ops.com, ops-lead@finco.com, oncall@carrier-networks.com
Date: 2027-12-08T09:55:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Zero-downtime cutover rehearsal: bridge notes, warmstart, and rollback triggers

Pulled a short checklist together for the rehearsal — posting here so people on the bridge can reference quickly. I also attached the bridge logs bundle after the rehearsal window.

Pre-bridge (08:30–08:55)
- Dashboard snapshots captured (baseline SST, 1h and 24h)
- Mirror test executed (carrier confirmed packets arrive)
- ACLs verified against test IP list (NET-784)

Warmstart execution (09:05–09:15)
- Seeded hottest prefixes from Acme export (Julie confirmed)
- Applied initial TTL=30s, monitor hits every 60s
- At 09:14 hit-rate reached 87% (short of 90% target) — extended TTL to 45s and re-evaluated

Traffic shift (09:20–09:35)
- Traffic ramped to 20% -> 50% in 5-minute increments; no 5xx spikes
- p50 latency jumped 1.6x at 20% ramp then stabilized to 1.1x within 4 minutes

Observation window (09:35–10:05)
- KV hit-rate stabilized at 92% by 09:43
- Small increase in background error rates from a downstream cache node (node-cache-5) — auto-remediation did not trigger; ops manual restart performed at 09:48

Rollback drill (10:05–10:10)
- Simulated 5xx spike by toggling a feature gate upstream; rollback playbook enacted successfully and traffic shifted back in 90s. No customer-facing errors observed.

Attachments: bridge-logs-20271208.tar.gz (contains collector summary, mirroring packet counts, and initial priming traces)

Notes / action items:
- Karthik: look into auto-remediation rules for node-cache-5 and tighten threshold for restart.
- Hannah: add a short step in section 3 of the runbook to explicitly validate the cache priming TTL ramp logic.
- Sean: let's debrief at 3pm PT — I can present the log highlights and propose a small amendment to the warmstart sequence.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, julie@acme-ops.com
Cc: ops-lead@finco.com, oncall@carrier-networks.com
Date: 2027-12-08T17:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Zero-downtime cutover rehearsal: bridge notes, warmstart, and rollback triggers — quick readout

Team —

Great rehearsal. Key takeaways for the exec and SRE on-call paths:
- Warmstart performed well after a short TTL bump; candidate default should move from 30s to 45s for initial priming when partner seeds are used.
- Rollback drill completed inside our 2-minute target (observability-to-action loop was the limiter).
- The cache node auto-remediation gap is actionable and not blocking — Karthik and engineering to patch threshold logic.

I uploaded a short readout to the runbook (link above) and attached the logs bundle. For leadership: we can greenlight a controlled production shift next week if the cache remediation and the brief runbook tweak (Hannah) are done.

Next steps (concrete)
1) Karthik: submit PR for auto-remediation threshold and schedule a <1h test with node-cache-5 by 2027-12-10 EOD.
2) Hannah: add TTL ramp step in runbook and run a doc-only review by 2027-12-09 noon PT.
3) Marissa: finalize bridge postmortem (one-pager) and circulate to Acme and Finco stakeholders.

If there are no escalations I will mark this rehearsal as successful and move to controlled production ramp planning.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bridge-logs-20271208.tar.gz
